parameters.determinism: All audit rules below are frozen so that any future replay of the same slices yields byte-identical decisions.

timestamp_rule.slice_identity: GDELT export filenames are YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.export.CSV.zip covering the preceding 15 minutes ending at HHMMSS UTC; every row inside must have DATEADDED equal to that bucket end (verified: both slices have exactly one distinct DATEADDED equal to the filename minute).
timestamp_rule.signal_timestamp: UTC naive timestamp t_sig = DATEADDED + 00:15:00 (the moment the slice is complete upstream). A record's signal becomes available no earlier than t_sig.
timestamp_rule.position_start_rule: First tradable bar with bar_start >= t_sig (contract rule 'positions begin no earlier than the next tradable bar'). For dailies that is the next calendar bar; no same-bar fills.
timestamp_rule.event_day_rule: SQLDATE is the CAMEO event day and lags DATEADDED (measured: same-day 1149/1184 rows in the 2022 slice, 462/464 in the 2026 slice; backward lags of 7-366 days occur, e.g. 14 rows dated 20210809 inside the 20220809 slice). An event-window rule that joins on SQLDATE alone therefore leaks staleness; any downstream consumer must declare a max SQLDATE lag or scope joins to DATEADDED. Both slices show backward-only, never forward, SQLDATE relative to DATEADDED (verified field check: no SQLDATE > DATEADDED date).
timestamp_rule.mention_counts: NumMentions (col 32), NumSources (col 33), NumArticles (col 34) are slice-relative; they must be consumed as per-slice levels or deltas keyed by GLOBALEVENTID across slices, never as cumulative history (verified present in 100% of rows in both slices).

dedup_rule.identity: (DATEADDED, normalized_source_url). URL normalization is deterministic: lowercase scheme and host, drop default ports (:80/:443), drop fragment and trailing '/', strip query params matching utm_*|fbclid|gclid|mc_cid|mc_eid, collapse repeated '/' in path, percent-decode reserved chars once.
dedup_rule.within_slice: Keep exactly one row per identity; when keys collide keep the row with the lexicographically largest (NumArticles, NumMentions, GLOBALEVENTID tuple) as canonical and log the rest as dropped_rows (deterministic). Measured collision density: 2022 slice 1184 rows -> 244 distinct keys (940 dropped, 79.4%); 2026 slice 464 rows -> 109 keys (355 dropped, 76.5%).
dedup_rule.across_slices: GLOBALEVENTID (verified unique within each slice: 1184 distinct/1184 rows and 464/464) is the event primary key; GLOBALEVENTID re-listed in a later slice updates mention-count deltas but never changes t_sig (first-seen DATEADDED wins). A NEW GLOBALEVENTID with the same identity key appends a new event row and never retro-edits the earlier row's t_sig (prevents double-counting one story as multiple fresh events).
dedup_rule.cross_day_stability: GLOBALEVENTID cross-slice reuse/dynamics UNVERIFIED (needs multi-day sample; single-slice uniqueness says nothing about cross-slice stability). Flagged as an audit-replay unknown, not assumed.

entity_rule.primary: Actor1Code (col 7), 3-char CAMEO code, when non-empty; measured present 1038/1184 (87.7%, 2022) and 424/464 (91.4%, 2026).
entity_rule.fallback: When Actor1Code is empty the fallback entity key is 'host:'+netloc(SOURCEURL) (distinct hosts measured: 119 of 244 distinct URLs in 2022 slice, 60 of 109 in 2026 slice), lowercased by the dedup normalization.
entity_rule.no_sec_identity: NO SEC identity of any kind: no CIK, ticker, companyconcepts, or submissions identity is defined or used, because data/manifest.json intentionally_omissions 'SEC bulk until a real declared User-Agent contact is provided' and no SEC file exists anywhere in data/. The ticker/cusip/name map is undefined; entity rule above is purely GDELT-CAMEO/host based.

audit_scope_facts.coverage_gap: Total local GDELT event coverage = 2 slices = 2 distinct ingest minutes (2022-08-09 03:00 UTC untrusted fixture + 2026-08-29 23:15 UTC canonical), i.e. effectively zero over the development window 2020-08-01..2023-12-31. Development-window backfill requires ~117k slice files (1219 days x 96/day) x ~30KB ~ 3.5 GB -- exactly the 'large GDELT history' the manifest intentionally omits until a hypothesis registers.
audit_scope_facts.what_this_audit_actually_establishes: That the two slices are structurally valid under a frozen 61-column map (cols_per_row 61 for all rows in both), that slice identity == DATEADDED == filename minute in both, that dedup and actor-coverage densities are computable and deterministic, that no field of interest needs imputation on these slices (mention/tone fields present 100%), and that the timestamp/dedup/entity rules above are implementable as stated.
audit_scope_facts.what_stays_unmeasured: Any coverage ratio over time, day-level event density, cross-slice GLOBALEVENTID stability, price-panel joinability under position_start_rule, and every downstream alpha question.

signal_timing: As frozen in parameters.timestamp_rule. Replay contract for any future run: fetch slices in ascending period order; for each slice assert every row's DATEADDED == period; apply dedup; emit events with t_sig = period + 15min; only then may a consumer compute positions starting at the next tradable bar. The audit asserts nothing about pre-2024 live availability beyond t_sig semantics because no historical slices exist locally yet.

first_falsification_gate.name: coverage_and_replay_feasibility_gate
first_falsification_gate.data_precondition: (a) Development-window GDELT export backfill exists locally under the manifest process (target >= 3 representative 15-min slices per calendar day across 2020-08-01..2023-12-31, upstream zips md5-verified against GDELT's md5-of-zip convention, with a per-slice manifest revision), and (b) a lawful point-in-time price panel covering the same window exists and exposes next-tradable-bar alignment per parameters.signal_timing. Without (a)+(b) the gate cannot run.
first_falsification_gate.then_falsify_if_any: (i) any row's DATEADDED != its slice period; (ii) any SQLDATE > slice period (forward-referencing event day); (iii) dedup output varies with slice processing order; (iv) two records share a GLOBALEVENTID with conflicting non-count fields across slices; (v) the frozen entity_rule maps >5% of rows to no entity (needs multi-slice evidence); (vi) position_start_rule produces bar_start < t_sig for any event. Any hit kills the replay-safety claim and thus the whole direction.

gate_result.verdict: gate_not_runnable: development-window backfill and point-in-time price panel are absent; direction stays 'blocked' until the data_precondition is satisfied through the manifest's collection process (no network work was permitted in this task, and none was done).
gate_result.partial_progress: The 2 available slices were audited in place (structure, timing identity, dedup density, actor coverage, field completeness) and pass those checks; the unregistered 2022 slice additionally demonstrates SQLDATE backward lag up to 366 days, so a naive same-day join rule is empirically falsified as a design choice even before backfill.

risks: Coverage conclusion could flip after backfill; nothing here should be read as 'GDELT is unusable'.
GLOBALEVENTID cross-slice stability and CAMEO code stability across GDELT schema revisions (the 61-col layout was verified on these two slices only) are untested risks.

The unregistered 2022 fixture has no provenance; if it turns out to be a third-party training/derivative dump rather than a raw GDELT slice, structural facts derived from it must be re-derived from canonical slices.
lastupdate.txt is a moment-in-time snapshot; upstream buckets churn within ~15 min (collection-time content already shows bucket 23231500 as next).
Any future LLM annotation layer (the workspace hypothesis) is explicitly out of scope here and would need its own falsification gate before any data-gate pass could promote this direction.
